correctness.rationale: The row/column parity identity follows exactly from unique even-neighbor best responses. It gives a necessary-and-sufficient bijection to parity vectors; all four cases and their exact coefficient counts, sparse extremes, and expected number of producers are proved without relying on experiments. The standalone exact checker independently tests 314,512 full profiles across 19 networks and GF2 rank/nullity consistency on 81 parameter pairs. A finite checker is corroboration, not an infinite proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: General linear-algebra procedures may enumerate finite instances, and for a fixed dimension pair can in principle list solutions. Neither an existence algorithm, rank formula nor invertibility criterion implies a preexisting published uniform symbolic distribution over all parameter values; the present claim is the specific closed coefficient formula and sparse-extremal counts. Stronger known coverage of even-even uniqueness is explicitly carved out.

evidence: For even-even dimensions Peters–Goldwasser–Young 2017 proves invertibility and therefore unique all-on equilibrium; this portion is covered.

For mixed/odd-odd parameters general finite-field linear algebra describes the solution affine space but need not give its Hamming-weight enumerator; published inspected formulas are rank/nullity conditions.
Gilboa–Nisan 2022 studies decision complexity, and Klimm–Stahlberg 2023 studies other patterns.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The assertion must be compared to stronger results by implication, not shared titles. Even-even uniqueness follows from a stronger existing switching-invertibility theorem and is explicitly acknowledged rather than marketed as new. For remaining families, knowing an algorithm or dimension gives total solution number but not how many solutions have each Hamming weight; different affine subspaces can have identical dimension and different weight distributions. The explicit four-regime producer-count distribution and sharp sparsest-equilibrium multiplicities were not found in inspected sources. Risk persists for unindexed odd-domination enumerators.

originality.rationale: The full symbolic producer-weight polynomial with sharp sparse-layer counts is not supplied by inspected primary game-theory, odd-domination, or Lights Out papers. The parity equation itself is known, and Peters et al. already imply the even-even singleton, both clearly acknowledged. General Sylvester/nullity formulas do not give the claimed Hamming-weight distribution. Remaining risk of an equivalent formula in unindexed graph-code literature is documented.
residual_risks: Caro–Klostermeyer–Goldwasser (2001) complete primary full text was not retrieved; accessible excerpts did not show covering formula.
An unindexed odd-domination, Lights Out, or coding-theory weight enumerator could coincide with the formula.
General finite-field methods imply all finite instances algorithmically; a stronger general symbolic enumerator, if located, would change novelty assessment.

value.rationale: For a natural infinite complete-row/column interaction family, the formula gives all production-level equilibrium multiplicities, not just feasibility or solution dimension, and exposes strong even-even versus odd-dimension parity transitions. The exact minimal producer count and its number of realizations solve a motivated equilibrium-selection/welfare statistic, while uniform equilibrium selection yields an exact expectation. This is a complete substantive classification rather than a routine parameter-specific test.
